prediction.primary_diagnosis: Choledocholithiasis / Biliary Calculi with Intermittent Obstructive Jaundice
prediction.clinical_reasoning: Scleral icterus, yellowish skin discoloration, and dark urine combined with episodic right upper quadrant or epigastric discomfort signify mechanical obstruction of the biliary outflow tract, predominantly caused by migration of gallbladder calculi into the common bile duct (choledocholithiasis). Prompt biliary decompression or extraction prevents suppurative cholangitis.
recommended_tests: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) — gold standard non-invasive imaging of biliary tree
Comprehensive Liver Function Tests (LFT) — total/conjugated bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), GGT
Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for therapeutic stone clearance if indicated
